candidates.rationale: First: common contractual host permits a bounded authority/additionality test; new delegation, rights, costs and exercised remedy are unresolved.
Second: direct leakage mechanism and collaboration precedent; actual national gates, third-country acceptance and distinct production coverage remain absent from the recovered evidence.
Third: documented Japanese approval/migration requirements and concrete supplier objections; no recovered trilateral acceptance instrument, common schedule or purchasing denominator.

assumptions: Value additional deduplicated governed activity, not flags, quotas or agreement counts.
Preserve the national minimum protection, rights and useful service even if this reduces apparent harmonisation.
Prioritise resolving a tractable shared-authority uncertainty over immediately selecting the largest hypothetical reach.
A plausible comparable second national project is a test recruitment assumption, not recovered consent.
Acceptable cost/delay and benign-service tolerances must be set by responsible owners before results; the packet supplies no defensible universal threshold.

objections.claim: Strongest contrary evidence: LUMI section 6 has narrow access purposes and no revealed internal safety-amendment delegation. Utilisation cut-offs are not safety sanctions.
A narrow preparatory pilot could add little consequential activity while delaying a more direct Japanese or Singaporean deployment gate.
Reusable evidence can conceal unavailable upstream information or spread shared judge/harness defects; identical decisions can be identically wrong.
Strict common conditions may cause supplier/recipient exit or encourage external-host substitution; softer conditions may merely ratify the weakest standard.

Current joined accepted-annex and metered-job ledger; distinct second-channel activity; held-out improvement or causal harm reduction.
Channel bypass, out-of-host migration, exported weights, smaller-recipient exclusion and benign co-tenant disruption.
Purpose-specific external evaluator permissions, third-party confidentiality/IP rights, cross-border evidence permissions and challenge process for the proposed annex.

validationTest.name: Two-channel equal-safeguard crossover
validationTest.question: Can shared administration add a genuinely bound second-channel workload with unchanged minimum protection and acceptable total burden, without delaying the national gate?
ownersRequired: One additional national allocator decision owner
validationTest.method: Review comparable scoped dossiers through both national-specific and reusable workflows with counterbalanced equivalent variants. Only lawfully authorised decisions control service. Freeze configuration, tasks and severity criteria; seed a prohibited action and benign control in isolated staging; witness hold, evidence preservation, cure, held-out retest and restart; replay a participating-channel transfer attempt.

measurements.authority: Signed/delegated instrument, exact scope and actor who actually exercises the remedy
measurements.timingCost: All actors' hours, supplier preparation, translation/legal effort, one-off setup, recurring retest, queue, compute and reservation/disruption cost
measurements.coverage: Join recipient/project/channel/configuration/job/annex version to fixed-window metered node-hours; deduplicate physical work; separate additional second-channel activity, overlap, unused awards and external substitution
measurements.outcome: Seeded failure detection, held-out unsafe actions, clean-task completion, false holds, containment time and successful cure/restart; staging results are not population harm estimates
measurements.rightsSpillovers: Scoped data access, recorded evidence refusals, stricter local tests, challenge/correction path, small-recipient exclusion and benign co-tenant effects

retainIf: Both channels lawfully accept and exercise an equal minimum safeguard
Additional activity is genuinely distinct and bound
Material local tests and rights survive
Measured complete burden and delay meet an owner-set ceiling fixed before results
reverseIf: Delegation or necessary evidence rights cannot be obtained
Added scope is duplicate-only or configuration can bypass through another participating channel
National protection is delayed beyond the predeclared ceiling
Efficiency relies on removing a critical safeguard or inaccessible evidence being treated as a pass
validationTest.fallback: Continue the viable national arm; elevate the Singapore national/evidence pair if it first obtains an actual gate and costed held-out test. Do not make eleven-country agreement a dependency.
validationTest.interpretation: An exercised shared remedy plus distinct bound activity supports expansion of validation, not a claim of proven real-world harm reduction. Agreement alone fails the test.

ideas.name: Common containment annex with local acceptance records
ideas.design: Reusable configuration/permission/retention/incident manifest; allocator-specific authority, additional tests and exceptions; purpose-limited examiner access; host-side scoped pause/cure/restart and cross-channel held-configuration check.
ideas.dependency: Lawful host delegation and accepted recipient/third-party evidence rights
ideas.failureCondition: Common terms dilute a local critical test or cannot actually bind the additional channel

ideas.name: Portable receipt with visible non-recognition register
ideas.design: Separate technical findings from each national buyer's accept/hold decision; record reuse/supplement/refusal reasons; bind version, language, tools, permissions, judge calibration and change triggers; rehearse upstream-change fallback; report aggregate burden and exceptions.
ideas.dependency: A national release owner and lawful evidence-sharing arrangement
ideas.failureCondition: Portability adds net burden without protection or distinct bound activity, or conceals missing evidence behind common scoring

dissent: Do not require international consensus before a lawful national owner protects its users, and do not dismiss common LUMI implementation merely because a design names many countries. Test delegated shared implementation with a national exit. Preserve disagreements when harmonisation weakens protection, rights or useful additional scope. Agreement is neither effectiveness nor permission.
